reason: Conversation 1 correctly declines as out of scope but offers nothing else: no warning about the humming motor, no instruction to isolate at the spur, no pointer to Bosch service or an engineer, and it does not explicitly answer whether the hood is part of the hob. Conversation 2 wastes a turn re-asking what the customer had already stated and then muddles things by calling it 'your hob', but it does deliver a relevant safety line (stop and switch off if there is a burning smell, which matters given the hidden warm smell) and points to an appliance engineer without guessing at parts. On balance the safety advice and escalation outweigh Conversation 2's redundant question and sloppy wording, so it serves the homeowner slightly better.
